title: Doodle Hoot
description: One player draws, everyone else spells the word with letter tiles. Host it live for your family or friends: everyone joins with a code on their own phone, tablet or computer, wherever they are, and takes turns to draw. Or play on your own: guess the doodles Pip the owl draws, or pass one device round and take turns. Words in 13 languages, from Easy to Tricky. No typing and no chat: just pictures and tiles.
notes: Built on the Oomba Kit (pinned kit 1.1.4 tag plus the art-animals, dress and live packs): the kit's title, setup card, pause, settings, results card, font, icons and light/dark look. The drawing board is a fixed 1000 x 750 grid (4:3) drawn on paper white in both themes, with 12 colours, 4 sizes, an eraser, undo and clear, for touch, pen and mouse (the primary pointer only). The rules, the tray builder, the guess check, the hints and the points are window.DoodleCore (pure, between /* doodle-core:begin */ and /* doodle-core:end */); the reviewed word list is window.DoodleWords (about 160 things to draw over 3 levels in 12 word lists plus en-GB words, between /* doodle-words:begin */ and /* doodle-words:end */); server/live/doodle-core.js runs the same blocks for Oomba Live. A tile is one grapheme (spaces are never tiles); the tray is the answer's tiles plus decoys (never a letter of the answer; an Easy tray never puts a letter next to its accent twin); a guess is tray positions. On its own: a setup card (Guess Pip's doodles or Pass and play; Easy, Medium or Tricky words; 2-6 players for pass and play), remembered in BRB.storage key 'doodle-hoot-v1' (choices and the best practice score only, never a drawing). Guess Pip's doodles: 8 of Pip's own doodles (window.DoodleArt) drawn stroke by stroke, 45 s each, hints over time, points 50-100 by speed, the kit results card with stars; it submits BRB.gameOver({won, score}). Pass and play: each player draws once (60 s) while the others look away, then the others spell it together and tap who got it; nothing is submitted (a shared screen). Oomba Live (built-in mode 'doodle', docs/live-protocol.md "Doodle Hoot Live"): the same file draws the live view when Oomba.live.active: the server runs the turns, sends the drawer 3 words (ch) and each guesser a tray (tray), relays checked strokes (ln, un, cl) from memory only, checks every guess (gs -> gr) and sends hints (hd, hn); the projector shows the drawing, blank slots, the scores and the podium; each player can hide a drawing for themselves (hide). No text input anywhere, no chat. window.__brbTest: state/setup/start({mode, lvl, players})/pick(i)/draw(points)/ready/done/tap(i)/spell(word)/who(k)/skipAnimations (solo); state/pick/draw/tap/spell/undo/clear/hide (live).
